core_proofs: Finite single-buyer quasilinear screening with finite ordered types, positive probabilities, bounded nonnegative quality, outside option zero and menu commitment. Prove direct-menu equivalence only for this single-agent maintained class, weak IC/IR and explicit participation/report tie convention. Do not claim unique implementation from weak IC.

Prove finite IC iff monotone quality and adjacent lower/upper utility-increment inequalities; telescope to all global constraints. Derive minimal rents with low IR and adjacent downward IC binding, then the exact finite virtual-surplus identity. Prove global optimality, exclusion and bunching, not only FOCs.

Continuum bounded monotone allocation IC/envelope equivalence by pairwise inequalities and Riemann sums, including jumps; derive rent integration and virtual surplus with explicit positive-density and convex-cost regularity. Prove the original uniform case globally. No unsupported general continuous ironing algorithm.

Risk-neutral lotteries: preserve all interim utilities by replacing a report lottery with its mean quality/payment; Jensen yields weakly lower convex expected cost. Explain participation timing, ex-post losses and nonconvex-cost counterexample without asserting a global optimum for that counterexample.

Explicit competitive posterior-wage signaling model: two types, continuous education, observed signal and type-dependent costs. Define pure PBE with Bayes on path and competitive wage as maintained pricing condition (or fully derive wage competition). Do not misapply finite sequential-existence theorem to continuous signals.

Fully characterize all pure pooling and separating education outcomes. Formally define equilibrium-dominated types via strict payoff comparison over sequentially rational/competitive responses and the Intuitive Criterion. Prove elimination of every pure pooling and excess-education separating equilibrium, plus survival of the least-cost outcome. Restrict uniqueness to pure education outcomes, not off-path beliefs or all mixed strategies.

Productive education changes net marginal signaling costs. Prove revised interval and refinement under positive net costs, zero-net-cost boundary failure of strict selection, and lack of finite high-type best response when productive return exceeds private marginal cost. Beliefs at the zero-net-cost boundary must respect refinement while allowing high type indifference.
